testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located inside:
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that stop the vehicle are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time it takes for the brakes to work after you press the brake pedal
The distance between the brake pedal and the floor
The amount of air pressure used to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The time it takes for the brakes to work after you press the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Air takes time to move through the air lines to reach the brakes. Air brakes do not work instantly. There is usually a delay of at least half a second between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes start to work.

questions.question: When you are about to go down a hill, you should shift into a ____ gear.
questions.explanation: Before going down a hill, shift into a low gear. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster as you go downhill.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light comes on in a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Test the brakes while driving, but keep going if everything seems fine.
Drive with the hazard lights on.

questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on in a vehicle with air brakes, you should stop and park the vehicle as soon as possible. You need to stop safely while you still have some braking power.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Pull out the air brake knob.

questions.explanation: To make a normal stop in a vehicle with air brakes, press the brake pedal down.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: What color light shows that a vehicle's ABS is not working?
questions.explanation: On vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS), a yellow warning light tells the driver that the ABS is not working.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, the rods move the slack adjusters when air pressure enters the brake chambers. This happens when the driver:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, turning the brake camshafts.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997, and other vehicles with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1998, must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: What does an air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
It moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks in an air brake system. An air compressor governor controls the air compressor.

questions.question: Front brake limiting valves usually have two markings. What do they say?
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve. It has two settings: "normal" and "slippery."

questions.question: What should you do with air tank drains?

options.text: Only use them when it is wet outside.
Use them to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use them to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Air in the brake system contains water and oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. You must open the air tank drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What do Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) do?

options.text: They reduce a vehicle's braking power.
They work with your normal brakes and do not reduce braking power.
They do not work well on large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They work with your normal brakes and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works alongside your normal braking system. It does not change your braking power. ABS only activates when your wheels are about to lock up.

questions.question: What color are the ABS malfunction lamps?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow warning lamps. They alert you when the braking system is not working. Know where your vehicle's lamp is before you drive.

questions.question: Is a low air pressure warning signal required on vehicles with air brakes?
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: At what pressure should the low air pressure warning signal activate?
questions.explanation: The warning signal should activate before the air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi. This signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: When is an alcohol evaporator most important?
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what happens if one system leaks?

options.text: It will always affect the second system
It may not affect the second system
It causes the second system to leak

questions.correctAnswerText: It may not affect the second system
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?
questions.explanation: Many large commercial vehicles use air brakes. Air braking systems use compressed air to work.

questions.question: What do air tank drains help do?

options.text: They should not be used in cold weather
They remove water and oil from the air tanks
They send air to the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the air tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and oil. This can damage the system if it builds up. Air tank drain valves help remove water and oil.

questions.question: What can happen if you do not drain air tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air builds up in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause brakes to fail.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using them together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator helps prevent ice buildup in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: What should you do if the low pressure warning light comes on while driving?

options.text: Stop where you are and park.
Leave the roadway and park as soon as safely possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the roadway and park as soon as safely possible.
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning light comes on, you must leave the roadway and park safely as soon as possible. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving but have the brakes fixed within a week.
Pull over and check the brakes right away.
Call a mechanic while you are driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the brakes right away.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop your vehicle immediately while you can still control the brakes. Check and repair the brakes as soon as possible.
